_note: MH-21 — the single source of truth for WHICH RAVENCLAUDE COMPONENTS ACTUALLY WORK ON WHICH HOST. Created 2026-07-28 by the multi-host audit. Before this file, every surface that needed the answer either hardcoded it (generate-dashboards.py's _HOOK_CAPABLE_HOSTS) or, more often, silently assumed 'everywhere' — which is how the Pipeline tab came to imply guardrails on hosts that run none, and how Heimdall came to report an unwatched perimeter as clean. A per-component annotation would have been ~20 copies of the same few facts, each free to rot independently; ONE map keeps them honest together.
_contract: `supported` is a claim about whether the component RUNS on that host today, in this repo, as wired by `scripts/ravenclaude`. It is NOT a claim about whether the host is capable in principle — Codex is the worked example: it speaks the hook contract natively and would run hooks fine, but nothing wires them, so `supported` is false and `blocked_by` says why. When a host gains an install path, update this file; do not add a second list somewhere else.
_provenance: verified = confirmed in-repo this session by a visible tool call. docs-verified = read from the host's own documentation this session, url given. inferred = neither; MUST be verified before anything is built on it.

hooks.what: PreToolUse / SessionStart / Stop guardrails — the tribunal, guard-destructive, runaway brake, layout gate, dod gate.

copilot.how: repo-level .github/hooks, wired by `ravenclaude install`, envelope translated by hooks/copilot-hook-adapter.sh
copilot.caveat: PLUGIN-level hooks never fire (github/copilot-cli#2540), which is why they ship repo-level. Tool-name VALUES are lowercase and are normalised in the adapter (f55039ec) — before that fix the tribunal and web guard were silent no-ops.

codex.blocked_by: no install path — `scripts/ravenclaude` has zero Codex references, so nothing wires hooks. The CONTRACT is already compatible (identical events, stdin fields, hookSpecificOutput envelope, exit-2 blocking, and Codex reads hooks/hooks.json in the plugin root directly), so this needs an installer, NOT an adapter.
codex.also_missing: CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and CLAUDE_SESSION_ID are absent — Codex passes cwd/session_id via stdin JSON. _emit-event.sh no-ops without the project dir, so no hook event is ever written even once hooks fire.
codex.note: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT and CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA ARE supplied by Codex as legacy-compatibility names — an earlier claim in this repo that they were not was wrong and is corrected in knowledge/codex-cli-customization.md.

cursor.blocked_by: no adapter and no install path. Cursor reportedly has its own hooks API (.cursor/hooks.json); unverified.
cursor.basis: verified (absence in-repo); the Cursor hooks API itself is inferred

codex.install_path_when_built: $REPO_ROOT/.agents/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md — Codex scans .agents/skills in EVERY directory from cwd up to the repo root, then $HOME/.agents/skills, then /etc/codex/skills, then bundled. SKILL.md needs name+description frontmatter (same shape as .claude/skills), so the existing skills project across unchanged.
codex.basis: docs-verified 2026-07-28 (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills) — upgraded from [inferred]. NOTE: multiple third-party guides claim `.codex/skills`; the primary source says `.agents/skills`. Trust this row, not a blog.
